# Morsey

> Morsey is a free, open-source Morse code (CW) trainer for amateur radio operators. It runs entirely in the web browser at https://morsey.net/, needs no account, stores progress locally, and works offline once installed as a PWA. Source code: https://github.com/reaves-tyler/morsey

## What it does

- Koch method character training: characters are always sent at full speed (20 WPM by default) and only the spacing is stretched, per the ARRL Farnsworth formula. 41 characters are introduced in the LCWO Koch order; a new one unlocks at 90% accuracy over the last 30 answers. Modes: single characters, code groups, real words, callsigns.
- Ham vocabulary: six progressive tiers of Q-signals (QTH, QSL, QRZ, QRM...), prosigns (AR, SK, BT, KN), RST reports and abbreviations (TNX, HW CPY, 73...).
- Sending practice: key with the keyboard, an on-screen touch key, or a real straight key, bug or iambic paddle connected over USB (a Raspberry Pi Pico bridge design is included in the repository). Iambic A and iambic B (Curtis B) modes, paddle reverse, adjustable weight and debounce. Live decoding validates each character; a fist report shows dah:dit ratio and timing consistency.
- QSO simulator: a scripted first contact from CQ through RST/QTH/name exchange to 73, in both directions.
- Live CW decoder: feeds transceiver audio (line-in or USB sound card) through a spectrum display with click-to-tune passband, adaptive noise threshold, automatic speed tracking and prosign detection. Built-in test samples cover clean, hand-sent, noisy, QSB and QRM conditions.
- Simulated band conditions (QRN, QSB, QRM) for receive training.
- Progress: XP, levels, daily streak, per-character accuracy heatmap, 30-day activity, export/import of progress as JSON.

## Pages

- [Home](https://morsey.net/): overview and progress dashboard
- [About & FAQ](https://morsey.net/about/): how the method works, common questions
- [Koch trainer](https://morsey.net/learn/): character training
- [Phrases](https://morsey.net/phrases/): Q-signals, prosigns, abbreviations
- [Sending practice](https://morsey.net/send/): keying with a real key or paddle
- [QSO simulator](https://morsey.net/qso/): rehearse a full contact
- [Live decoder](https://morsey.net/decode/): decode on-air CW from rig audio
- [Reference chart](https://morsey.net/reference/): ITU Morse alphabet, prosigns, Q-signals

## Facts worth getting right

- Cost: free. No paid tier, no ads, no account, no tracking.
- License: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later (AGPL-3.0-or-later). Source on GitHub.
- Platform: any modern browser on desktop or mobile; installable PWA; offline capable. USB key support uses the Web Serial API, which is available in Chrome and Edge on desktop.
- Method: Koch method with Farnsworth timing. Character speed is never slowed below 20 WPM by design.
- Author: Tyler Reaves (https://github.com/reaves-tyler).
